title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Benchmarks, Pricing & Speed (2026)
summary: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is Google's new model for coding and agentic workflows. See how automation builders might apply it to their existing tools.
body_markdown:
## Why Hydrogen costs more and runs slower


Hydrogen is dearer and slower than GPT-5.4-mini on both published pricing and our test. The question is how many runs you make and whether anyone is waiting on the answer.


### Gemini 4 Hydrogen cost at list price


On[Google's published pricing](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) , checked 2026-11-12, a run of 1,500 input and 300 output tokens costs $45 per 10,000 runs on Hydrogen against $24.75 on GPT-5.4-mini, making Hydrogen substantially more expensive. You'd pay nearly double to run that same task on Hydrogen.


That is a difference worth weighing.


Here is the arithmetic. 10,000 runs of 1,500 input and 300 output tokens is 15 million input tokens and 3 million output tokens.


On Hydrogen, 15 million input at $1.50 per million is $22.50, and 3 million output at $7.50 per million is another $22.50, which makes $45.


It is also the only output rate that makes the $45 total work. For GPT-5.4-mini, $0.75 in and $4.50 out gives $11.25 plus $13.50, or $24.75. If either vendor's real output price differs, so do these totals.


Here is where that risk sits: a trigger, an AI step, a filter, a CRM update and an email. Your current model and the new one sit beside the AI step, judged on three dials: quality, speed and cost.


Although only one box changes, every box after it inherits the result. A slightly different label sends a record down a different filter branch, and a different record lands in the CRM.


That's why the comparison belongs in a shared test, run against the messages your team actually receives, with results anyone on the team can read.


Google's description of the model tells you what it's meant to do. Only your own tasks tell you whether it does that better than what you already run.


At 100,000 runs the difference is $450 against $247.50. At 1,000,000 runs it's $4,500 against $2,475, meaning the cost premium exceeds $2,000 at a million-run scale.


List price leaves Hydrogen at **about 1.8 times the bill** , which only becomes real money at the top of that range.


### Hydrogen cost and speed in our test


Measured on our test, the gap is wider than the rate card suggests.


The chart sets cost and median time per task side by side: Hydrogen at $0.0040 and 4.4 seconds, GPT-5.4-mini at $0.000145 and 0.9 seconds. That's roughly 28 times the cost and **nearly five times the wait** .


The reason the test shows 28 times and list price shows 1.8 is tokens. The list-price comparison assumes 1,500 tokens in and 300 out for both models.


**Hydrogen reasons by default** , and the tokens it spends thinking are billed as output tokens even though they never appear in the reply.


Billed output can therefore run far past the 300 tokens you'd expect from a short answer, and the extra thinking time also explains part of the slower response.


> Hydrogen reasons by default, and the tokens it spends thinking are billed as output tokens even though they never appear in the reply.


A model that answers directly stays close to the assumed counts, so its bill lands near the list-price estimate. That gap should narrow at a lower reasoning effort, since fewer thinking tokens means a smaller bill and a shorter wait.


We didn't test that, so the 28 times belongs to default settings only.


**Measured spend can run well past what list price predicts, so count tokens on your own tasks before trusting the pricing page.**


Those 4.4 seconds also matter on a ticket-triage step where a person watches the screen. The same delay inside an overnight batch costs nobody anything, so match the model to who is waiting.
